questions.question: The minimum number of links in a single degree-of-freedom planar mechanism with both higher and lower kinematic pairs is
questions.explanation: Given: A planar mechanism has both lower and higher kinematic pairs and is of single degree of freedom . Formula used (Kutzbach criterion for planar mechanisms): [latex] F = 3(L - 1) - 2J_1 - J_2 [/latex] Where, F = degree of freedom L = number of links J1 = number of lower pairs J2 = number of higher pairs For single degree of freedom: [latex] F = 1 [/latex] Assume minimum possible number of links: [latex] L = 4 [/latex] Substitute values: [latex] 1 = 3(4 - 1) - 2J_1 - J_2 [/latex] [latex] 1 = 9 - 2J_1 - J_2 [/latex] [latex] 2J_1 + J_2 = 8 [/latex] This equation can be satisfied with a valid combination of lower and higher pairs. Therefore, minimum number of links = 4
questions.explanation_html:
Given:
A planar mechanism has both lower and higher kinematic pairs and is of single degree of freedom.

Formula used (Kutzbach criterion for planar mechanisms):
[latex] F = 3(L - 1) - 2J_1 - J_2 [/latex]

Where,
F = degree of freedom
L = number of links
J1 = number of lower pairs
J2 = number of higher pairs

For single degree of freedom:
[latex] F = 1 [/latex]

Assume minimum possible number of links:
[latex] L = 4 [/latex]

Substitute values:
[latex] 1 = 3(4 - 1) - 2J_1 - J_2 [/latex]
[latex] 1 = 9 - 2J_1 - J_2 [/latex]
[latex] 2J_1 + J_2 = 8 [/latex]

This equation can be satisfied with a valid combination of lower and higher pairs.

Therefore, minimum number of links = 4

questions.question: A project consists of three parallel paths with mean durations and variances of (10,4), (12,4) and (12,9) respectively. According to the standard PERT assumptions, the distribution of the project duration is

options.A: Beta with mean 10 and standard deviation 2
options.B: Beta with mean 12 and standard deviation 2
options.C: Normal with mean 10 and standard deviation 3
options.D: Normal with mean 12 and standard deviation 3

questions.explanation: In PERT (Program Evaluation and Review Technique), it is assumed that: : The project duration is governed by the critical path (the longest expected duration among all paths). The project duration follows a normal distribution approximately, due to the Central Limit Theorem. Step 1: List the mean durations and variances for each path: Path 1: [latex] \mu_1 = 10, \ \sigma_1^2 = 4 [/latex] Path 2: [latex] \mu_2 = 12, \ \sigma_2^2 = 4 [/latex] Path 3: [latex] \mu_3 = 12, \ \sigma_3^2 = 9 [/latex] Step 2: Identify the critical path Since the critical path is the one with the maximum mean duration: [latex] \max(\mu_1, \mu_2, \mu_3) = \max(10, 12, 12) = 12 [/latex] We have two paths with mean duration 12. As per PERT, among these, the path with the larger variance is considered for total project variance (more conservative estimate). Thus, select Path 3: [latex] \mu = 12, \ \sigma^2 = 9 [/latex] Step 3: Write the distribution The project duration approximately follows a normal distribution: [latex] N(\mu, \sigma^2) [/latex] i.e., [latex] N(12, 9) [/latex] Or equivalently: Mean = 12, Standard Deviation = [latex] \sqrt{9} = 3 [/latex].
questions.explanation_html:
In PERT (Program Evaluation and Review Technique), it is assumed that:
:
The project duration is governed by the critical path (the longest expected duration among all paths).
The project duration follows a normal distribution approximately, due to the Central Limit Theorem.

Step 1: List the mean durations and variances for each path:
Path 1: [latex] \mu_1 = 10, \ \sigma_1^2 = 4 [/latex]
Path 2: [latex] \mu_2 = 12, \ \sigma_2^2 = 4 [/latex]
Path 3: [latex] \mu_3 = 12, \ \sigma_3^2 = 9 [/latex]

Step 2: Identify the critical path
Since the critical path is the one with the maximum mean duration:
[latex] \max(\mu_1, \mu_2, \mu_3) = \max(10, 12, 12) = 12 [/latex]
We have two paths with mean duration 12.
As per PERT, among these, the path with the larger variance is considered for total project variance (more conservative estimate).
Thus, select Path 3:
[latex] \mu = 12, \ \sigma^2 = 9 [/latex]

Step 3: Write the distribution
The project duration approximately follows a normal distribution:
[latex] N(\mu, \sigma^2) [/latex]
i.e.,
[latex] N(12, 9) [/latex]
Or equivalently:
Mean = 12, Standard Deviation = [latex] \sqrt{9} = 3 [/latex].

questions.explanation: Let l be the length of both plates and assumed that surrounding between two large plate be as surface 3. [latex] \begin{aligned} A_{1} &=A_{2} \\ F_{11}+F_{12}+F_{13} &=0 \; \; \; \left(F_{11}=0\right) \\ F_{21}+F_{22}+F_{23} &=1 \; \; \; \left(F_{22}=0\right) \\ F_{31}+F_{32}+F_{33} &=1 \; \; \; \left(F_{33}=0\right) \\ \text{By symmetry }F_{31}&=F_{32} \\ 2 F_{31}&=2 F_{32}=1 \\ F_{31} &=F_{32}=0.5 \\ A_{1} F_{13} &=A_{3} F_{31} \times \l \times w) \times F_{13} \\&=\left(2 l \sin 10^{\circ} \times w\right) \times 0.5 \\ F_{13} &=\sin 10^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex] By cosine law [latex] \begin{aligned} b^{2} &=l^{2}+l^{2}-2 l^{2} \cos 20^{\circ} \\ \Rightarrow \quad b^{2} &=2 l^{2}\left(1-\cos 20^{\circ}\right) \\ &=2 l^{2} \times 2 \sin ^{2} 10^{\circ} \\ &=4 l^{2} \sin ^{2} 10^{\circ} \\ b &=2 l \sin 10^{\circ} \\ F_{12} &=1-F_{13}=1-\sin 10^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex] By symmetry [latex] \begin{aligned} F_{12} &=F_{21}=1-\sin 10^{\circ} \\ &=0.826 \end{aligned}[/latex] Alternatively: [latex] \begin{aligned} F_{12} &=F_{21}=1-\sin \frac{\theta}{2} \\ &=1-\sin \left(\frac{20^{\circ}}{2}\right)=0.826 \end{aligned}[/latex]
